title: Entropy-based fidelity credit allocator: product brief and rollout playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document describes the Entropy-Based Fidelity Credit Allocator (EFCA), a product component that dynamically assigns finite fidelity credits to tenant requests based on request entropy, service-level objectives (SLOs), and marginal economics. EFCA is intended to reduce customer-visible fidelity regressions while improving token cost efficiency across hosted and dedicated deployments.

This brief includes: rationale, allocation mechanics, API/contract examples, policy knobs, rollout plan, observability requirements, SLO impact analysis, and pricing examples.

Goals

- Protect response quality for high-information requests while reducing average per-token cost.
- Provide deterministic, auditable credit allocation that maps to existing billing/crediting systems.
- Enable gradual rollout with telemetry and regression guardrails.

Scope

- Applies to: hosted API and Dedicated (gateway layer). Not enabled for Private VPC until customer consent and contract amendment.
- Applies to fidelity-sensitive features: multishot chat, code generation, and structured output where fidelity materially affects correctness.
- Not a replacement for fidelity bundles or flat per-token pricing; EFCA augments existing bundles with behavior-driven credit steering.

Key definitions

- Fidelity credit: unit used by runtime to select higher-cost execution paths (larger model variant, less quantization, longer KV cache retention). One credit ~= 1 premium token-worth-of-cost in baseline economics.
- Request entropy: a scalar estimate of the information content of the request payload and context window (0..1). Higher entropy means more uncertain and high-value text.

Design principles

1. Signal-first: use robust, explainable signals (entropy, historical route fidelity, tenant fidelity SLAs).
2. Marginal economics: allocate credits where marginal improvement in quality justifies marginal token cost.
3. Auditable decisions: every allocation decision must emit an allocation record for billing and audits.

Allocation mechanics (high level)

1. Input signals per request: request_entropy, tenant_priority_score, route_fidelity_budget, recent_quality_trend, fallback_compatibility_flags.
2. Score = w_e * entropy + w_p * priority + w_q * quality_trend (weights configurable per tenant pool).
3. Compute marginal_expected_quality_gain(score) using an internal mapping model (calibrated by lab evals).
4. If marginal_expected_quality_gain * value_per_quality_point >= marginal_cost_of_credit, allocate N credits (0..max_per_request).

Policy knobs (examples)

- w_e, w_p, w_q: weights for entropy, priority, and quality trend (float).
- max_credits_per_request: integer cap (default 10).
- fallback_reserve: percentage of tenant daily credits reserved for emergency fallbacks (default 5%).
- entropy_thresholds: low/medium/high buckets that map to default allocation bands.

API and allocation record contract

Allocation is exposed as a synchronous pre-filter endpoint used by the routing/gateway layer. Contract (JSON example):

Request (POST /v1/allocator/allocate)
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "route": "chat.v1",
  "request_entropy": 0.73,
  "context_length": 2048,
  "priority": "standard",
  "recent_quality_trend": -0.02
}

Response
{
  "allocation_id": "alloc-20261014-abc",
  "credits_allocated": 4,
  "allocation_reason": "entropy_high_margin_positive",
  "predicted_quality_gain": 0.12,
  "estimated_extra_cost_tokens": 520,
  "expires_at": "2026-10-14T12:14:23Z"
}

Every allocation must produce an allocation record for billing and audit topics in the following minimal shape (pub/sub JSON string):
- allocation_id, tenant_id, route, credits_allocated, baseline_variant, allocated_variant, reason, marginal_cost_est, predicted_quality_gain, timestamp, trace_id

Configuration examples (gateway feature flag + tenant override)

1) Global feature flag (yaml):
features:
  efca_enabled: true
  efca_default_weights:
    w_e: 0.7
    w_p: 0.2
    w_q: 0.1
  efca_max_credits_per_request: 10

2) Tenant override (json stored in tenant config service):
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "efca_enabled": true,
  "weights": {"w_e":0.8, "w_p":0.15, "w_q":0.05},
  "max_credits": 6,
  "fallback_reserve_pct": 0.05
}

Observability and telemetry requirements

- Surface the following dashboards: allocation-rate, credits_consumed_per_tenant, average_predicted_quality_gain, allocation_reasons_breakdown, chargeback_estimate_by_route.
- Alert if: daily credits consumption > 120% of forecast, average_predicted_quality_gain drops below 0.03 for 24h, or allocation error rate > 0.5%.
- Add taggable traces: allocation_id and trace_id must propagate through gateway -> runtime -> billing pipeline.

SLO and gating criteria for rollout

- Quality regressions: no customer-facing drop > 5 percentage points in eval pass rate on critical prompt sets for any top-10 tenant during canary.
- Latency: pre-filter allocation latency must be < 12ms p95 in hosted mode. If allocation latency causes overall request p95 to exceed SLO by > 5%, disable synchronous allocation and fall back to sampled async allocation.
- Cost: predictable billing — forecasted marginal spend must be within +/- 10% of actual spend for the first 30 days for canary tenants.

Rollout plan (phased)

Phase 0: Lab (complete)
- Generate calibration datasets linking entropy to quality gains for target models and sequence lengths.
- Build mapping models and sanity checks.

Phase 1: Internal canary (2 weeks)
- Enabled for internal tenants and Redwood-owned demo accounts. Validate allocation records, telemetry, and billing pipeline.

Phase 2: Opt-in customer canary (4–6 weeks)
- Invite 5 customers across SMB and mid-market with different workload shapes. Collect objective evals (pre/post) and revenue impact. Baseline: 2M tokens/day combined.

Phase 3: Default-on for new tenants / opt-out for existing (8 weeks)
- Roll EFCA as default for new tenants. Provide easy tenant override and UI in Console.

Phase 4: Enterprise expansion and Private deployment consent (Q3-Q4)
- Offramp for regulated customers: EFCA can be disabled or run in dry-run mode with allocation records only.

Risk analysis and mitigations

- False positives (allocating credits where no quality improvement): Keep conservative mapping model and cap max_credits_per_request. Review high-frequency reasons.
- Billing disputes: Provide allocation record exports and a Console view of allocation decisions. Implement reconciliation job to compare estimated marginal cost vs actual billing.
- Latency impact: implement fast-path cache for recurring allocation decisions keyed by (tenant, route, entropy_bucket).

Pricing and billing ties

- EFCA does not change baseline token pricing. Instead, credits map to premium charge events. Billing schema: for each allocation record, emit a provisional charge_line with {tenant_id, allocation_id, estimated_extra_cost_tokens}. Final charge reconciled daily with actual runtime cost multipliers.
- Playbook for refunds: if predicted_quality_gain < 0.02 and estimated_extra_cost_tokens > 250, mark allocation as eligible for automated credit refund and notify tenant.

Examples (worked scenarios)

1) High-entropy code generation request
- entropy 0.92, tenant standard plan, predicted_quality_gain 0.18 -> allocate 8 credits -> runtime uses a less-quantized variant and extended KV retention -> customer sees fewer compile/regression failures.

2) Low-entropy routinized text completion
- entropy 0.12, predicted_quality_gain 0.01 -> allocate 0 credits -> cost saved, output identical quality.

Operational runbooks (short)

- Allocation spread spike (>200% of forecast): 1) notify billing and SRE, 2) set tenant-level throttle to cap daily credits, 3) enable aggressive entropy thresholds for 1 hour. Owner: billing (pager duty).
- Allocation endpoint errors >0.5%: 1) flip gate efca_enabled=false globally, 2) fail-open to 0 credits, 3) paged to runtime-oncall. Owner: eng-platform.

Open items and product decisions required

- Accounting model: reconcile provisional credit charges into token billing buckets vs new fidelity SKU. Decision owner: finance.
- Console UX: build allocation audit timeline in Console. Decision owner: DX/Product.
- Lab calibration cadence: re-evaluate mapping model quarterly or when new major model variant is onboarded. Owner: applied-ml.

Appendix: calibration example (pseudo)

- Lab eval summary mapping: for model variant A -> quality_gain per added credit approximated by a logistic curve fit on labeled evals.
- Example mapping table (excerpt):
| entropy_bucket | avg_quality_gain_per_credit | recommended_credits |
| low (0-0.33)   | 0.02                       | 0                      |
| medium (0.34-0.66)| 0.06                     | 2                      |
| high (0.67-1.0) | 0.15                       | 6                      |

- Implementation note: store per-model, per-seqlen calibration matrices in the model-profile service.
